newsitem.title: UK: Rebel shareholder says Greycoat must talk.
newsitem.headline: Rebel shareholder says Greycoat must talk.

text.p: Rebel Greycoat shareholder Brian Myerson said on Thursday that the British property company would be forced to talk to rival Moorfield Estates about a proposed merger between the two following the three-week adjournment of a vote on the possible break-up of the company.

Myerson's Active Value Advisors advises rebel investment fund shareholders UK Active Value Fund, IMP UKAV Inc and Chaddesley Investments, which control 11 percent of Greycoat's shares and had put forward a resolution to sell its assets.
"The (Greycoat) board will be forced to sit down and look at the Moorfield proposals," he told reporters after the meeting.
Myerson said he was delighted that shareholders had voted to adjourn his original proposal to sell off the company's assets.
"We are delighted -- it was the right thing for the shareholders to vote in favour (of an adjournment)," he said, adding his main object was to create value for shareholders.
Myerson said the Moorfield proposals, which have so far been rejected by Greycoat as being too vague, had the backing of holders of 40 percent of Greycoat shares
He said these holders had already seen Moorfield's 40-page document and expressed their support for it, adding that he was "supportive" of both the proposals and the Moorfield management.
"We are supportive of Moorfield in terms of its proposals and we want it (the board) to sit down with them," he said.
"We expect Moorfield to refine its proposals over the next couple of weeks," he added.
Greycoat management representatives were not immediately available for comment.
